title: Implement pre clip midrange peaking bell voicing filter
description:
Create Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.h and Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.cpp implementing a 2nd-order RBJ peaking (bell) filter applied before the non-linear clip stage.

Requirements:
- Class MidVoicingFilter with prepare(double sampleRate), reset(), and process/processBlock methods on a single mono channel; buffers/state allocated only in prepare().
- Center frequency mid_freq constrained to 500-1200 Hz, driven by a multiplicative SmoothedValue (strictly-positive frequency domain).
- Gain mid_amount up to +9 dB boost, driven by a linear SmoothedValue (dB domain). Fixed Q_m = 0.9.
- RBJ peaking-bell biquad coefficients recomputed on sample-rate change and on smoothed parameter movement; no allocation in process.
- Denormal-safe recursive state (flush tiny values / denormal-safe accumulation).
- No heap allocation, locks, file IO, or string construction inside process().

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/ (existing DSP module conventions and namespace from phases a/b)
- CMakeLists.txt (how DSP sources are registered; do NOT modify it in this task)
- JUCE/modules/juce_audio_basics for juce::SmoothedValue (read only; never modify anything under JUCE/)

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.h and Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.cpp exist and declare/define class MidVoicingFilter
MidVoicingFilter uses a multiplicative SmoothedValue for mid_freq (500-1200 Hz) and a linear SmoothedValue for mid_amount (dB, up to +9 dB)
The filter is a 2nd-order RBJ peaking bell with fixed Q_m = 0.9
RBJ coefficients are recomputed on sample-rate change and denormals are flushed in the recursive state
cmake --build build --target ShredBoost compiles Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.cpp without errors
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/TightFilter.h, Source/DSP/TightFilter.cpp, Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.h, or Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.cpp
allocate heap memory, take locks, or construct strings inside the audio process loop

allowed: add private biquad state and coefficient fields
choose internal helper for RBJ peaking coefficient math
forbidden: change the DSP processing chain order
